title: An adaptive dynamic parameter replacement strategy to defend against hidden backdoor attacks in federated learning
assignee: Lianyungang Zhiru Huixin Technology Co ltd

pse.problem: Federal learning (FL) systems are vulnerable to hidden back door attacks due to their black box nature for servers. These attacks manipulate model parameters in a way that they show malicious behaviors under specific conditions and remain normal otherwise.
pse.solution_function: A self-adaptive dynamic parameter replacement strategy monitors less updated model parameters using small-scale clean data sets held by each client, and replaces these parameters to eliminate hidden back doors.
pse.solution_structure: Each client has a small-scale clean data set and the global model. The system includes a parameter monitoring module for tracking model parameter updates in the rounds.
pse.solution_implementation: The system dynamically identifies and replaces the k% parameter at the bottom of the hidden back door attack, ensuring normal model training and enhancing the system's robustness.
pse.effect: The solution effectively copes with hidden back door attacks in federal learning systems, improving their safety and stability.
